about: A purchase in Thune v1 (buy within the Card), as KIFF keeps it and every other side reads it: the case and what its digest signs, its states, KIFF's execution lease, the live authorization's rules, the approval the apps draw, the owner's signed answer, and the signed receipt. Amounts are integers in the currency's minor units. Every word the owner reads comes from KIFF in `words`; the apps never compose or decide. Written by hand, as data, until KIFF's batch A writes it from its own test; then copied here byte for byte, as kiff-agent-draft-from-hold.json is.

case.about: The case KIFF builds from what it and planque read at the checkout (`Checkout.Same`), never from the taf's words. Every field here is signed: the digest is SHA-256, hex, of the object's canonical JSON (RFC 8785, as runtime/src/cloud/jcs.ts writes it). Any change to a signed field is a new `version` with a new digest, which voids the earlier signature and releases its reservation; a total that stays within `price.rule` is the one change that isn't. `price.total` is `lines` plus `shipping` plus `tax` (tax 0 when the line amounts include it), `price.max` is `total` plus `rule.up_to` (or `total` with no rule), and `grant.cap` equals it. `path` is the case's, never the page's: a merchant chosen for `token` that asks for a card number ends with nothing sent. `delivery` is signed, so an address changed after the decision sends nothing. `valid_for_seconds` is fixed at 900: an approved, unused case ends 15 minutes after its decision. `merchant.category` is the merchant category code, for the receipt and the Record; `grant.categories` are the issuer's own category names, which the card's spending controls take. `merchant.match` is how the live authorization knows it's this shop, not only this kind of shop: the issuer's merchant network id when the case has one, otherwise the issuer's merchant name, folded (lower case, letters and digits only, accents removed), containing `name_key`; and the merchant's country. So the words can say "at this shop". `merchant.stripe_profile` is the seller's Stripe profile a token names (`profile_…`): read only from the case's own checkout site (`merchant.site`, on the grant's sites, over https), in planque's signed checkout block, never from the taf; any other host's is refused. `path: token` needs it, and a case without one is refused as it's built; a `card_fill` case has none. `route: existing_method` (and `grant.kind: existing_method`) isn't in v1: KIFF refuses a case with it until that route has its own design.

facts.about: Read beside the case and never signed: re-read freely, shown as information. A change here makes no new version.

states.about: Three statuses, kept apart: the case's, the money's and the order's (payment, order and receipt are reconciled separately). `unknown` is a state, never a guess: a case whose outcome is unknown can't execute again until reconciliation says `ordered` or `not_ordered`, and a retry after it is the same case id, never a new case.

case.means: waiting for the owner (ask_each_time, or outside the Card's limits)
decided: the owner signed this version, or KIFF found it within every limit; the room is reserved
the owner refused; no room was reserved
a material change made a new version; this one's signature and reservation are void
no decision, or no execution, within its time; the reservation is released and any card cancelled
KIFF's lease is held by one execution; nothing else may execute this version
the execution may or may not have placed an order; every further execution is refused until reconciled
an order exists for this case (reconciled or confirmed); it never executes again
it ended with nothing charged; `ended` says why

leave_unknown.about: Reconciliation alone moves a case out of `unknown`.
leave_unknown.to_done: an order exists for the case
leave_unknown.to_approved: no order exists, the money's status is `none` or `reversed` (no authorization standing on the card), and `valid_until` hasn't passed: the same case id may execute again
leave_unknown.otherwise: not_bought, its room released, its card cancelled and its token revoked

decision.about: How a case was decided, in its digest's record, never re-decided the other way. The room is reserved in the same transaction: a conditional write that fails if another purchase took the room first, and then the decision doesn't count (`ended: room_taken`, or held for the owner in within_limits). `approved_once` is set by the live authorization's single approval, as a conditional write in the same transaction as its answer.

execution.about: KIFF's execution lease: one execution per case version, taken by conditional write; a second call (a double tap, an agent's retry, two runs) finds it and gets the first execution's state, never a second checkout. planque's mark armed before the click stays as a second guard. The card is made only after the decision (the fingerprint, or KIFF's within-limits check), never before. `card` links it: the issuer's card id, set once, which the live authorization finds the case by. The issuer card's own metadata carries the case id and the permit's `jti`, so a card with no case can be found and cancelled. Neither the card nor a token outlives the decision's `valid_until`.

token.about: For `path: token`: the token is made from the case's card, only after the decision, and scoped as the card is. It's a secret: never logged, never shown to the taf, kept only for its life, and revoked when the case ends, used or not. A merchant chosen for a token that asks for a card number ends with nothing sent (`ended: card_number_asked`).
rules: expires_at is no later than the decision's valid_until
seller is merchant.stripe_profile, the signed value only
before live: when Stripe gives the profile's business name or site, it matches merchant.match as the case opens; until then the live authorization's exact shop match is the fence

authorization.about: The issuer's live authorization: a lookup in KIFF's store, never a judgement, no model, person or outside call. It approves only when every check holds, at most once per case, and declines everything else, including any internal error. A timeout is a decline: the card's own controls (single use, `grant.cap`, `grant.categories`) are decline-shaped, so the issuer's fallback can't approve anything the case doesn't allow. The decision is logged with the case id, never a card number.
approves_only_if: the card is the case's (one card per case)
the case is approved, within valid_until, with its lease held
the merchant's issuer category is in grant.categories
the issuer's merchant is the case's: merchant.match.network_id when set, otherwise its folded name contains merchant.match.name_key; and its country is merchant.country
the amount fits price.max minus what is already authorized
an incremental authorization or re-authorization fits within price.max
never: a second approval for the case
a force capture (flagged to the owner; the Card's buying pauses)
records: the issuer's merchant name and category
verification result: authenticated, exempted (by whom) or required

approval.about: What the apps draw on a held purchase, every line in KIFF's words. Show more is closed each time and opens every line, and the toggle then says `show_less`; the signature covers the version, so approving with the lines closed approves exactly those lines. Never offers extra room. `lines` and `charges` together add up to `total`; `delivery` is drawn under the total.

words.reason: Your Card asks you each time.

answer.about: The owner answers the hold KIFF opens for the case (a held call: the `exception id` line is that hold's id, never the case's), with `approve-once` (the approval key, behind the fingerprint), which decides the case, or `reject` (the device key), which refuses it. Within limits there's no hold and no answer. The signed bytes are kiff.answer.v1's newline-joined lines as the apps sign them today (kiff.answer.v1, tenant, exception id, answer, next step, note hash, hold version, signed at), then one more line, `purchase:<case_id>:<version>:<digest>`, so the signature binds this case's digest; a purchase never has a browser line. KIFF refuses an answer whose purchase line isn't the case's current version and digest (stale), or that has none.

answers.approve-once: decides the case: approved, its room reserved

receipt.about: KIFF's signed receipt, kept in the Record: what was decided and what happened, `unknown` said as unknown. Signed by KIFF (Ed25519, `kid`) over the canonical JSON of `value`. The issuer's merchant name and category sit beside the case's, so a mismatch is visible; on `path: token`, the case's side carries the `stripe_profile` the token named, so a profile that paid someone else shows. A placeholder `sig` here; the reader checks the shape and that `digest` is the case's. `path` says which way it paid, and `words.card` is that path's line. `words.order` is the order's state as the shop confirmed it (`words.shipping` is kept for the delivery's, once there is one). `approver.self` is whether the reader is the approver, and `method` how they approved: device_biometric or security_key.
